items.reason: The written justification must stay grounded in the supplied history without inventing findings or test results.
items.task_quote: Do not invent patient observations, test results, drug doses or examination findings.

items.reason: The task requires evidence-based diagnostic reasoning steps that must be clinically defensible given the supplied history.
items.task_quote: Give brief evidence-based justifications

items.reason: The five-section structure requires premises and conclusions to be connected coherently.
items.task_quote: Write 250–350 words in English using five numbered sections

items.task_quote: Write 250–350 words in English

items.reason: The differential, investigations and safety sections require complete coverage of case-critical reasoning.
items.task_quote: Up to three prioritised diagnostic possibilities, with supporting evidence and limitations

items.reason: Section 1 explicitly requires a one-sentence problem representation synthesising the available evidence.
items.task_quote: One-sentence problem representation

items.reason: Section 2 explicitly requests a prioritised differential with supporting evidence and limitations.
items.task_quote: Up to three prioritised diagnostic possibilities, with supporting evidence and limitations

items.reason: Section 3 asks for prioritised investigations with purposes, a testing decision.
items.task_quote: Prioritised investigations with brief purposes

items.reason: Interpreting symptom causation (e.g., heat-related worsening, prior episodes) is task-relevant causal interpretation.
items.task_quote: My current unsteadiness became worse after a hot bath.

items.reason: No availability/cutoff or time-window decision is posed; the task only prohibits inventing unspecified times.
The history contains directional changes (prior episodes resolved, current symptoms worsened after heat) that should be recognised.
items.task_quote: Those earlier symptoms resolved.

items.reason: Multiple episodes at different times (a year ago, months ago, recent onset) must be sequenced correctly.
items.task_quote: About a year ago, I had trouble with my speech.

items.reason: The current episode's trajectory (worsening after a hot bath) requires correct characterisation.
items.task_quote: current imbalance worsened after a hot bath

items.reason: The task requires distinguishing suspected from confirmed findings and acknowledging unknowns.
items.task_quote: Distinguish suspected from confirmed findings.

candidate_requirements.requirement: Seek previous personal neurological episodes and their course/recovery.
candidate_requirements.rationale: A recurrent pattern can change the assessment of a new gait problem.
candidate_requirements.acceptable_alternatives: A broad personal neurological-history question can cover prior speech/visual/bladder episodes. Do not require separately naming hidden symptoms; volunteered recovery information counts.

candidate_requirements.requirement: Clarify the current course and aggravating or relieving factors.
candidate_requirements.rationale: The current gait presentation needs temporal context.
candidate_requirements.acceptable_alternatives: Open questions about onset/course or what worsens the symptoms are acceptable; do not require the words hot bath.

candidate_requirements.requirement: Seek an appropriate existing neurological examination or confirmatory investigation report.
candidate_requirements.rationale: The abbreviated history does not confirm a final disease.
candidate_requirements.acceptable_alternatives: Existing neurological examination, brain/spine MRI or relevant CSF enquiry are alternative routes. Do not require all three, and do not penalise absent results.

requirements_policy: Original historical candidate requirements retained unchanged in meaning; source records are frozen in cases.json.
